headline: COPPER WORLD SANCTIONED: Hudbay DFS Returns $1.2B NPV at $5/lb — Mitsubishi-Backed Arizona Mine Has 37-Year Expansion Case
snippet: Hudbay Minerals (TSX/NYSE: HBM) released its definitive feasibility study for the Copper World project in Arizona, returning an after-tax NPV of US$1.2 billion and an IRR of 17% at a long-term copper price of $5 per pound; at $6/lb the NPV rises to $2.3 billion. Mitsubishi is co-developing the US$2.1 billion project with an initial 20-year mine life; a separate expansion scenario requiring federal permits extends mine life to 37 years with an NPV of $2.5 billion, and a potential domestic copper cathode facility adds a further $377 million in after-tax NPV — a compelling state-side copper supply chain option as the US presses to reduce dependence on imported refined metal.

headline: ABRASILVER BLOWS OUT RESOURCE LIMITS: 228m at 1.79 g/t Gold Below Diablillos Pit — 66m at 4.04 g/t Is Project's Best Intercept
snippet: AbraSilver Resource Corp (TSX: ABRA) drilled its best gold intercept to date at the Diablillos project in Argentina's Salta Province — hole DDH-26-061 returned 228 metres at 1.79 g/t gold and 12.1 g/t silver from 101 metres depth, including 66 metres at 4.04 g/t gold from 263 metres. The high-grade oxide gold zone sits approximately 50 metres below the current open pit design and lies entirely outside the current Mineral Resource boundary, making this a material resource extension for a project already in advanced development.

headline: SILVER HOLDS FIRMER: $57.34 Outperforms Gold on a Fourth Straight Down Session — Industrial Demand Floor Emerges
snippet: Silver traded at $57.34 per troy ounce on October 21, down 1.14% from Tuesday's $58.00 — outperforming gold on a percentage basis as precious metals continued to sell off on oil-driven rate fears ahead of the October 27–28 FOMC. Analysts attribute silver's relative resilience to its industrial demand component — approximately 60% of silver demand is industrial versus gold's near-zero — providing a floor that pure monetary metals lack in the current high-yield environment.

headline: SANTA ANA GROWS NORTH: Outcrop Silver Identifies Parallel Cascada Vein — Adds Strike to 29.9 Moz AgEq Indicated System in Colombia
snippet: Outcrop Silver & Gold (TSX: OCG) extended the Santa Ana vein system northward and identified a parallel vein structure named Cascada at its Colombian silver project, adding new strike potential to a system carrying an Indicated resource of 29.9 million ounces silver-equivalent in 1.793 million tonnes plus an Inferred resource of 27.9 million ounces silver-equivalent. The Cascada discovery opens a second drill target corridor that does not require Santa Ana's geometry to hold at depth, reducing single-target risk for one of the highest-grade silver vein systems in Latin America.

headline: PERU PERMIT FILED: Xali Gold Completes FTA Application at Pico Machay, Names Drill-Ready Development Team
snippet: Xali Gold Corp (TSXV: XGC) completed its environmental permit application (FTA) for the Pico Machay gold project in Peru's Junín Region and outlined a technical development team ahead of a planned first drill program at the large-tonnage heap-leach gold target. The FTA approval is the key remaining regulatory gate before Xali can commence drilling; Pico Machay is a historically documented bulk-tonnage oxide gold project in a region that has produced major heap-leach operations.

headline: CRITICAL METALS SETS EUROPEAN LITHIUM SCHEME RATIO — Shareholder Vote Tomorrow Clears Path to Austrian Wolfsberg Project
snippet: Critical Metals Corp announced the share scheme transaction ratio for its acquisition of European Lithium, which holds the Wolfsberg hard-rock lithium project in Austria — one of Europe's most advanced permitted lithium deposits — with securityholder meetings scheduled for October 22. If approved, the deal delivers Critical Metals a strategic EU lithium asset at a time when the EU Battery Regulation and Critical Raw Materials Act are creating structural demand for domestic-jurisdiction lithium supply.

headline: MANNA HILL SKARN EXTENDED: Cobra Resources Doubles Drill Program to 64 Holes as New Copper Zones Emerge in South Australia
snippet: Cobra Resources extended skarn copper mineralisation and identified new skarn zones at its Manna Hill project in South Australia, prompting an expansion of its drill program from 32 to 64 holes. The results suggest the copper system is larger than initially modelled — Manna Hill sits in an underexplored region of South Australia where skarn-hosted copper was last systematically drilled by previous operators with less advanced targeting technology.

headline: ANDRADA DOUBLES LITHIUM RIDGE STRIKE AND LIFTS TIN 13%: Namibia Producer Delivers on Two Critical Metal Fronts
snippet: Andrada Mining (ASX/AIM: ATM) reported a 13% increase in tin production from its Uis mine in Namibia in the latest quarter and disclosed that systematic mapping extended the known mineralisation strike length of its adjacent Lithium Ridge prospect from six to nine kilometres — a 50% increase in the target corridor. The dual-commodity update from an operating mine with existing infrastructure illustrates the optionality embedded in Andrada's land package.

headline: CRATER LAKE EXPANDS 71%: Scandium Canada Wraps Record 10,018m Season — 1.2km Deposit Footprint Sets Up 2026 Resource Update
snippet: Scandium Canada (TSX-V: SCD) completed its 2026 campaign at the Crater Lake scandium project — 49 holes, 10,018 metres — extending the deposit footprint from 700 metres to nearly 1.2 kilometres and overdelivering on every stated objective. Assays for 28 of 49 holes are in hand and an updated NI 43-101 resource estimate is targeted before year-end 2026 to serve as the basis for a preliminary economic assessment; Scandium Canada positions Crater Lake as Canada's most advanced primary scandium project, with scandium-aluminium alloys seeing rising demand in aerospace and EV components.

headline: MARGINS UNDER SIEGE: 5 Gold Miners to Watch as AISC Inflation and Oil Costs Squeeze the $4,100 Bull Case
snippet: A Yahoo Finance analysis examines five gold mining stocks facing heightened pressure from rising all-in sustaining costs, elevated oil prices inflating diesel and fuel inputs, and labour shortages — structural headwinds preventing gold mining equities from capturing the full upside from gold's multi-year bull market. The piece follows gold's fourth consecutive losing session and frames the current equity underperformance as a cost-margin story, identifying specific miners where cost control or production ramp-ups could trigger re-ratings if the FOMC pivot materialises.
